report.summary: Chunk 2 of slice.py: focus unit resolution, neighbor expansion with egress gating, shell boundary stops, and withheld reporting.
risks: withheld_map.setdefault | medium | First role to withhold a rel names it, but if a later role has a different rule, the setdefault will keep the first role, potentially misrepresenting the reason for withholding. Settled by verifying that the rule for a given rel is always the same regardless of role, or by intentional design.

symbol path callee/caller emission | medium | The code emits callee_section and caller_section as strings that are appended to neighbors, but the section strings are defined once and reused for each unit; if no units exist, the section string is still defined but not used. This is harmless but could be cleaned up.

doc edges shell_stops counting | low | For doc edges, if r == rel, it is skipped (no increment). But if r != rel and r not in modules, shell_stops is incremented. This matches the import edges behavior. However, the comment says 'shell_stops += 1' for doc edges when r != rel and r not in modules, but the code does that. No risk.

withheld_lines | low | The withheld_lines list is built but never used in this chunk; it is presumably appended to slice_text later. If it is not included, the breadcrumb is missing. Settled by checking the rest of the function.

claims.text: ``modules[rel]``, by contrast, is assigned only INSIDE that guard -- so membership in ``modules`` is exactly "is in the declared center".
claims.why: The chunk does not show where modules is assigned or the guard; the claim about assignment is not verifiable from this code alone.

claims.text: This also keeps every downstream ``_units_of``/``_skeleton`` call scoped: they re-read off disk and know nothing of the index, so the filtering has to happen here, before a rel reaches them.
claims.why: The code filters dep_rels and caller_rels using 'r in modules' before passing them to _units_of and _skeleton (lines 332-333, 345-346).

claims.text: a link is not an import, and the roles must stay distinguishable in the ``included`` provenance
claims.why: documents_out and documented_by are kept separate from dep_rels/caller_rels, and later emitted with distinct role strings 'documents' and 'documented_by'.

claims.text: the symbol path below feeds dep_rels/caller_rels into ``graph.callees``/``graph.callers``, which match IDENTIFIER TOKENS. Prose is full of words that look like identifiers, so a document merged into those sets would manufacture call edges out of English.
claims.why: The code only enters the symbol path if 'not is_doc' (line 373), so documents are excluded from the callee/caller resolution.

claims.text: Both maps are absent from an index built without documents, so this is inert by construction on the default path.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the index construction or default path; the claim about absence cannot be verified from this code alone.

claims.text: Gating each emitted unit's module closes that.
claims.why: The _emit_ok function is called before adding each unit to neighbors (lines 418, 422, 438, 452), checking the egress rule for the module.

claims.text: Floor (secret-only) applies in every lane; the default-deny allow-list only in an untrusted lane.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the implementation of slice_egress_rule or the policy/lane parameters; the claim about floor vs allow-list is not verifiable from this code alone.

claims.text: Per file, so the deny_content first-match-break cannot poison a whole slice and every hit is attributable to one path.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the implementation of slice_egress_rule; the claim about per-file evaluation cannot be verified from this code alone.

claims.text: ``not is_doc``: the symbol path is the CALL-GRAPH path, and a document has no call graph.
claims.why: The symbol path is guarded by 'if symbol and focus_unit is not None and not is_doc' (line 373), so documents are excluded.

claims.text: ``graph.callees`` resolves identifier TOKENS, and for a document focus the resolver's same-file table is that document's own headings -- so any prose word matching a heading title would be emitted as a "callee"
claims.why: The chunk does not show the implementation of graph.callees or the resolver; the claim about heading matching cannot be verified from this code alone.

claims.text: A document's real relations are its links, and they are emitted below in their own section under their own name.
claims.why: Document relations are emitted later in the code (lines 455-470) as separate sections labeled 'DOCUMENTS' and 'DOCUMENTED BY'.

claims.text: the resolver does not go through them: ``SymbolResolver.resolve`` reads ``defs_by_file`` directly, so a name that binds to a SHELL unit returns that unit and its full body lands in the CALLEES block -- straight past the gate that exists to stop exactly this.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the implementation of SymbolResolver.resolve or defs_by_file; the claim about direct reading cannot be verified from this code alone.

claims.text: Keying the resolver cache by scope fixes the cause; this fixes the CLASS, so no future resolver provenance (a stale cache, a hand-built resolver, a caller that omits scope_key) can reopen it.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the resolver cache or scope_key usage; the claim about fixing the class cannot be verified from this code alone.

claims.text: Rejections are COUNTED into the same shell_boundary_stops the module path reports
claims.why: The code adds n_callee_shell and n_caller_shell to shell_stops (line 411).

claims.text: EGRESS GATE at emission: a callee body / caller signature is withheld if its file trips the gate, even when it reached here via the resolver.
claims.why: The code filters callee_hits and caller_hits using _emit_ok (lines 418, 422).

claims.text: Same egress gate, same order (``_emit_ok`` BEFORE ``_skeleton``, so a file that trips the floor is never read into the emitted text).
claims.why: The document layer code calls _emit_ok before _skeleton (line 462).

claims.text: Lowest keep rank (0) so a token budget sheds prose before it sheds code.
claims.why: The document layer neighbors are appended with 'keep': 0 (line 468), while code neighbors have keep 1 or 2.

claims.text: sorted() for determinism: the withheld block and its breadcrumbs are order- independent of dict insertion / set iteration.
claims.why: The code sorts withheld using sorted() with a key (line 476-478).

claims.text: Fail-loud breadcrumb IN the slice text (matching the spirit of shell_boundary_stops, but inline so the model sees it): a withheld neighbour leaves a marked gap, never an unmarked one it might hallucinate across.
claims.why: The code builds withheld_lines list with a header and per-file lines (lines 482-485).

claims.text: This block is kept LAST and is NEVER dropped by the budget -- degrade sheds neighbours, not the gate's own report.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the budget mechanism; the claim about never being dropped cannot be verified from this code alone.

observations.what: The function _rule_for caches results per rel, but _emit_ok calls _rule_for each time; caching is beneficial.
withheld_map.setdefault will keep the first role that withholds a file, even if a later role has a different rule. This may cause the withheld breadcrumb to show an incorrect role for the rule.
The docstring for the symbol path says 'graph.callees' uses identifier tokens, but the code does not show the implementation; the claim is uncheckable.
The variable 'withheld_lines' is built but not used in this chunk; it is presumably appended to slice_text later. If not, the breadcrumb is missing.
